summary: Iteration 54 — SEC-002 header-based auth end-to-end verification (member Bearer + admin X-Admin-Token). Backend: 17/17 pytest assertions pass covering /api/ask/usage, /api/admin/ai-usage, /api/admin/ask/clear-usage (POST body), /api/admin/geo, /api/admin/ask/pending-review, /api/admin/calm/list. Frontend: 5 admin pages (/admin/ai-usage, /admin/geo, /admin/ask-review, /admin/calm, /admin/revenue) all render correctly and issue their API requests with X-Admin-Token header — ZERO `token=` in URL query strings. /ask page as a paid member loads sessions/usage via Authorization: Bearer header — ZERO `access_token=` in URL. /calm audio `.mp3` URL correctly retains ?access_token= (intentional, HTML audio cannot send custom headers). No auth breaks. Backwards compatibility with legacy ?access_token= and ?token= query params confirmed working.
critical_code_review_comments: SEC-002 implementation is now clean: middleware in server.py (_accept_bearer_access_token, lines 249-287) reads Authorization: Bearer and X-Admin-Token headers and injects them into the query_string ASGI scope, so downstream route signatures declaring `access_token: str` / `token: str` from Query keep working unchanged. Explicit query params still win over headers — good for the audio-tag legacy path.

api.js interceptor _attachAuth is scoped so X-Admin-Token is ONLY attached on /api/admin/* and /api/affiliate/* URLs (guarded by isAdmin check on config.url). Prevents accidental admin-token leak to public endpoints.

One tiny polish: server.py:266 still imports urllib.parse inside the middleware function on every request. Cheap but non-idiomatic; move to module scope. (Was flagged in iteration 53 too — not blocking.)

SEC-003 client IP source (previous iteration's CRITICAL finding — request.client.host still returns proxy pod IP in K8s ingress) is OUT OF SCOPE for this iteration but remains unresolved. Re-flag: /app/backend/routers/ask.py vote_popular should read cf-connecting-ip / x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip before falling back to request.client.host, mirroring _GEO_HEADERS pattern in server.py.
